extended: 2026-11-15: +6 domain-map sources (geva2021ffn, park2023linear, agarwal2026transfer, oozeer2025transfer, chen2025stitching, slocum2025belief; abstracts extracted under runs 4c02bf49b492711e and c04d1866bda27360, re-resolved under ac3ac4bc3af5f4db) and +4 KB entries (P06, P07, O11, O12)
purpose: Citation-grounded knowledge base of what model edits and perturbations do, for the direct-model-edit skill's cascade (ground, route, localize, edit/subtract, verify). Every KB entry's evidence array cites ids defined here; every source was resolved and ledgered server-side under the research run.

field_semantics.intervention_space: weight / activation / input — where the perturbation is applied. This KB's center of gravity is weight space; no input-space paper met the explicit-bridge bar and none is retained.
field_semantics.propagation: Blast radius of the perturbation's effects beyond its intended target: none (methodological entry, no behavioral claim), local (effects concentrated on the target behavior), cascading (effects spread to related behaviors/dimensions), global (effects across the model).
field_semantics.entry_type: principle = falsifiable generalization with at least 2 independent supporting papers; observation = single-paper or below-bar finding, recorded with its scope.

domain_link_verdict: The exact term 'perturbation probing' is used by the literature for exactly the practice the skill's premise names — observing the effects of interventions on model internals to identify what carries a behavior — but it is a 2026 coinage of one research line (Liu, Li & Wu, arXiv:2604.27401, with same-team secondary coverage from Unit 42 and the Cloud Security Alliance). The same practice predates the name and is carried by 'causal mediation analysis' (Vig et al. 2020), 'causal tracing' (ROME's intervention), 'activation patching' / 'interchange intervention' (Zhang & Nanda name the equivalence explicitly), and the knowledge-editing evaluation literature (Cohen, Zhong, Yao). The KB proceeds under this restated link.

sources.title: Perturbation Probing: A Two-Pass-per-Prompt Diagnostic for FFN Behavioral Circuits in Aligned LLMs
sources.authors: Hongliang Liu, Tung-Ling Li, Yuhao Wu
sources.full_text_verified: 2026-11-14: 29-page arXiv PDF extracted and checked against the KB's five seed-citing entries under research run aaf284255c0cc444
sources.term_sense: Coins 'perturbation probing': a diagnostic that perturbs FFN neurons to generate causal hypotheses and validates them by an intervention sweep; interventions are FFN-neuron ablation/amplification plus residual-stream direction injection (activation).
sources.def_quote: Perturbation probing generates task-specific causal hypotheses for FFN neurons in large language models using two forward passes per prompt and no backpropagation, followed by a one-time intervention sweep of about 150 passes amortized across all identified neurons.

sources.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
sources.authors: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov
sources.term_sense: Causal tracing (a causal-mediation intervention on activations) used to locate mid-layer FFN sites, then Rank-One Model Editing (ROME) applied to the feed-forward weights.
sources.def_quote: We first develop a causal intervention for identifying neuron activations that are decisive in a model's factual predictions. This reveals a distinct set of steps in middle-layer feed-forward modules that mediate factual predictions while processing subject tokens.

sources.title: Mass-Editing Memory in a Transformer
sources.authors: Kevin Meng, Arnab Sen Sharma, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov, David Bau
sources.term_sense: Batch (mass) knowledge editing: multi-layer rank-one-style updates at causal-mediator MLP sites, scaling single-fact editing to thousands of associations.
sources.def_quote: We develop MEMIT, a method for directly updating a language model with many memories, demonstrating experimentally that it can scale up to thousands of associations for GPT-J (6B) and GPT-NeoX (20B), exceeding prior work by orders of magnitude.

sources.title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
sources.authors: Damai Dai, Li Dong, Yaru Hao, Zhifang Sui, Baobao Chang, Furu Wei
sources.term_sense: Knowledge attribution (integrated gradients) identifying FFN 'knowledge neurons'; interventions suppress/amplify neuron activations and edit FFN output weights to update or erase facts.
sources.def_quote: we propose a knowledge attribution method to identify the neurons that express the fact. We find that the activation of such knowledge neurons is positively correlated to the expression of their corresponding facts.

sources.title: Investigating Gender Bias in Language Models Using Causal Mediation Analysis
sources.authors: Jesse Vig, Sebastian Gehrmann, Yonatan Belinkov, Sharon Qian, Daniel Nevo, Simas Sakenis, Jason Huang, Yaron Singer, Stuart Shieber
sources.term_sense: Causal mediation analysis for interpreting neural NLP: treats neurons and attention heads as mediators between input and output, intervening to measure total/direct/indirect effects. OpenAlex carries the v1 title 'Causal Mediation Analysis for Interpreting Neural NLP: The Case of Gender Bias'.
sources.def_quote: these methods can only measure whether the information exists, not whether it is actually used by the model. We propose a methodology grounded in the theory of causal mediation analysis for interpreting which parts of a model are causally implicated in its behavior.

sources.title: Editing Large Language Models: Problems, Methods, and Opportunities
sources.authors: Yunzhi Yao, Peng Wang, Bozhong Tian, Siyuan Cheng, Zhoubo Li, Shumin Deng, Huajun Chen, Ningyu Zhang
sources.term_sense: Knowledge/model editing survey; states the field's objective (the contract) and empirically analyzes method families, finding enduring issues. The contract quote anchors the llm_editing ontology concept (operator ruling 2026-11-07).
sources.def_quote: the objective of which is to efficiently alter the behavior of LLMs within a specific domain without negatively impacting performance across other inputs

sources.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
sources.authors: Gabriel Ilharco, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Mitchell Wortsman, Suchin Gururangan, Ludwig Schmidt, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Ali Farhadi
sources.term_sense: Task arithmetic: fine-tuned-minus-pretrained weight deltas ('task vectors') as composable, negatable directions in weight space.
sources.def_quote: A task vector specifies a direction in the weight space of a pre-trained model, such that movement in that direction improves performance on the task.

sources.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
sources.authors: Prateek Yadav, Derek Tam, Leshem Choshen, Colin Raffel, Mohit Bansal
sources.term_sense: Model merging as multi-vector task arithmetic; identifies and resolves parameter interference (redundant values, sign conflicts) when composing task vectors.
sources.def_quote: existing merging methods often ignore the interference between parameters of different models, resulting in large performance drops when merging multiple models

sources.title: Steering Language Models With Activation Engineering
sources.authors: Alexander Matt Turner, Lisa Thiergart, Gavin Leech, David Udell, Juan J. Vazquez, Ulisse Mini, Monte MacDiarmid
sources.term_sense: Activation engineering / ActAdd: steering vectors from prompt-pair activation differences, added to the forward pass at inference time.
sources.def_quote: activation engineering strategically perturbs activations at inference time

sources.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
sources.authors: Andy Arditi, Oscar Obeso, Aaquib Syed, Daniel Paleka, Nina Panickssery, Wes Gurnee, Neel Nanda
sources.term_sense: Single-direction mediation of refusal; direction ablation (erasure from the residual stream) and addition as a white-box intervention on refusal behavior.
sources.def_quote: we find a single direction such that erasing this direction from the model's residual stream activations prevents it from refusing harmful instructions, while adding this direction elicits refusal on even harmless instructions

sources.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
sources.authors: Fred Zhang, Neel Nanda
sources.term_sense: Activation patching methodology; explicitly names the practice's aliases and lineage: 'also known as causal tracing or interchange intervention ... (Vig et al., 2020)'.
sources.def_quote: Activation patching, also known as causal tracing or interchange intervention, is a standard technique for this task (Vig et al., 2020), but the literature contains many variants with little consensus on the choice of hyperparameters or methodology.

sources.title: Evaluating the Ripple Effects of Knowledge Editing in Language Models
sources.authors: Roi Cohen, Eden Biran, Ori Yoran, Amir Globerson, Mor Geva
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL) 2024
sources.term_sense: 'Ripple effects': the implications a single factual edit should have for related facts; an evaluation benchmark (RippleEdits) measuring whether weight-space editors propagate or preserve them.
sources.def_quote: injecting one fact (e.g. 'Jack Depp is the son of Johnny Depp') introduces a 'ripple effect' in the form of additional facts that the model needs to update (e.g. 'Jack Depp is the sibling of Lily-Rose Depp')

sources.title: MQuAKE: Assessing Knowledge Editing in Language Models via Multi-Hop Questions
sources.authors: Zexuan Zhong, Zhengxuan Wu, Christopher D. Manning, Christopher Potts, Danqi Chen
sources.term_sense: Multi-hop evaluation of knowledge editing: whether edited models answer questions whose answers should change as entailed consequences of the edits.
sources.def_quote: comprising multi-hop questions that assess whether edited models correctly answer questions where the answer should change as an entailed consequence of edited facts

sources.title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can Be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot
sources.authors: Elias Frantar, Dan Alistarh
sources.term_sense: One-shot pruning (and quantization-compatible) sparsification as a massive weight perturbation with computed compensation; measures the behavior preserved under global weight deletion.
sources.def_quote: large-scale generative pretrained transformer (GPT) family models can be pruned to at least 50% sparsity in one-shot, without any retraining, at minimal loss of accuracy

sources.title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
sources.authors: Mor Geva, Roei Schuster, Jonathan Berant, Omer Levy
sources.term_sense: Storage theory: transformer FFN layers operate as key-value memories (keys correlate with training-text patterns; values induce output-vocabulary distributions); no intervention — grounds the weight-space substrate that locate-then-edit methods write into. Abstract extracted in run c04d1866bda27360; resolved by DOI in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db.
sources.def_quote: feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary

sources.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
sources.authors: Kiho Park, Yo Joong Choe, Victor Veitch
sources.term_sense: Theory: the linear representation hypothesis formalized through counterfactuals, with provable connections to probing and steering and a non-Euclidean causal inner product; grounds the direction as the unit of intervention. Abstract extracted in run c04d1866bda27360; resolved in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db.
sources.def_quote: high-level concepts are represented linearly as directions in some representation space

sources.title: Cross-Architecture Steering Transfer in Language Models: A Systematic Empirical Study
sources.authors: Ayushi Agarwal
sources.term_sense: First systematic evaluation of cross-architecture steering-vector transfer: shared geometry is functionally exploitable conditionally, with a suggestive discontinuity near 1.7B parameters and sharp degradation below 0.8B. Abstract extracted in run 4c02bf49b492711e; resolved in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db.
sources.def_quote: shared LLM geometry is functionally exploitable, conditionally

sources.title: Activation Space Interventions Can Be Transferred Between Large Language Models
sources.authors: Narmeen Fatimah Oozeer, Dhruv Nathawani, Nirmalendu Prakash, Michael Lan, Abir Harrasse, Amirali Abdullah
sources.term_sense: Learned mappings of shared activation spaces transfer safety interventions (backdoor removal, refusal steering) across Llama/Qwen/Gemma families; smaller models can align larger ones. Abstract extracted in run 4c02bf49b492711e; resolved in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db.
sources.def_quote: safety interventions can be transferred between models through learned mappings of their shared activation spaces

sources.title: Transferring Linear Features Across Language Models With Model Stitching
sources.authors: Alan Chen, Jack Merullo, Alessandro Stolfo, Ellie Pavlick
sources.term_sense: Affine maps between residual streams transfer SAEs, probes and steering vectors across model sizes; semantic and structural features transfer differently. Abstract extracted in run 4c02bf49b492711e; resolved in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db.
sources.def_quote: cheap way to effectively transfer represented features between models

sources.title: Believe It or Not: How Deeply do LLMs Believe Implanted Facts?
sources.authors: Stewart Slocum, Julian Minder, Clément Dumas, Henry Sleight, Ryan Greenblatt, Samuel Marks, Rowan Wang
sources.term_sense: Belief-depth framework (generality, robustness, internal representations) applied to knowledge editing: mechanistic editing (AlphaEdit, a MEMIT-lineage null-space editor) fails to implant deeply while synthetic-document finetuning often succeeds. Abstract extracted in run 4c02bf49b492711e; full text (90 pp) verified in run ac3ac4bc3af5f4db.
sources.def_quote: simple prompting and mechanistic editing techniques fail to implant knowledge deeply
